key_insight: LLENS enabled an on-premises LLM agent to answer hospital-document questions with 97.2% accuracy using interactive tools, versus 81.3% with fixed retrieval.
clinical_relevance: The platform could support hospital document and administrative workflows inside closed networks, but patient-care benefits were not evaluated.
method: Deployed Kimi K2.6 on one server with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs inside a Japanese university hospital network.
Combined document-reading tools, a network-isolated sandbox, output self-checking, subagents, and saved procedures.
Compared document-access approaches and demonstrated five workflows using synthetic data.
evidence_signal: Across 180 hospital-document questions evaluated with 3 seeds each, interactive access outperformed fixed retrieval by 15.9 percentage points (95% CI 10.9–21.3).
watch_item: Document-question accuracy and synthetic demonstrations do not establish clinical safety or real-world workload reduction; the reported hardware requirements are substantial.
paper_title: The LLENS Platform for On-Premises Large Language Model Agents in a Japanese University Hospital: Development and Evaluation Study
